# Optimized benchmark results

Primary target: **Node 26.12.0 / o200k_base**. Bun 1.4.3 and cl100k are release-regression checks. All tables use five fresh processes; ranges are full process minimum–maximum, not confidence intervals. Ranks exclude the historical npm release.

**The legacy arithmetic mean is dominated by two large synthetic inputs. It does not establish a universal winner.** Realistic categories and repeated/32-variant modes stand separately in the [overview](experiments/OVERVIEW.md); every per-document median loss is listed there. The [interpretation](OPTIMIZED-FINDINGS.md) discusses losses and tradeoffs.

Host: benchmark-vm, 8 vCPUs presenting 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1360P, 15.54 GiB; linux/x64, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic. KVM VM, no CPU pinning/frequency control. The queue prevents our jobs from overlapping; shared-host scheduling, turbo, JIT and GC remain uncontrolled.

Encoding/decoding/counting use the original seven-input mean per process. Load excludes process startup. Memory is a separate settled one-pass phase, including byte-heavy decode; final/peak RSS include harness/corpus. See [all contenders and every input](experiments/LEGACY-node-o200k-RESULTS.md).

## Informational release comparisons

These selected runs compare the checkout with npm 4.0.3 only; they do not re-rank other competitors. Values below are legacy mean latency ratios: npm / checkout, so above 1 is a speedup. The linked tables include absolute latencies, load, and matching memory.

| Engine / encoding | Encode speedup | Decode speedup | Count speedup | Detailed evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| node / cl100k_base | 1.694× | 18.228× | 1.877× | [Timing and memory](experiments/LEGACY-node-cl100k-RESULTS.md) |
| bun / cl100k_base | 2.295× | 4.040× | 2.258× | [Timing and memory](experiments/LEGACY-bun-RESULTS.md) |
| bun / o200k_base | 2.031× | 4.100× | 2.055× | [Timing and memory](experiments/LEGACY-bun-RESULTS.md) |

## Decode and read all output

API-return timings read only result length and can leave decoded strings as lazy ropes. The [separate consumed-output comparison](experiments/CONSUMED-OVERVIEW-RESULTS.md) includes a checksum over every returned code unit, with [full absolute tables](experiments/CONSUMED-node-o200k-RESULTS.md). It measures decode plus the common consumer cost and is not pooled with API-return ranks.
